recap.text: Tipid guesses that King Rust, level 78 on his swamp yak Gonk, leveled on a ring of Divine Suffering and a necklace of Indelible Woe, which trades a random spell of the wearer's for one of a target's. Carl, who has the dead king's body in his inventory, now holds both. He tells Donut they do not need the necklace. Li Na asks about it, then refuses because she could lose her level-15 dreads, so it stays with Carl.

beats.headline: How a copycat levels
beats.text: King Rust has turned up as a war chief, riding a swamp yak named Gonk, and Donut's Size-Up reads him: level 78, dozens and dozens of spells, most at level one but some from 11 to 15, Protective Shell at 15 among them. How did he level so fast? Tipid says he likely has a ring of Divine Suffering for the stats and a necklace of Indelible Woe for the spells. It is in the same collection as the ring, and it trades a random spell of the wearer's for one of a target's; kill the target and it is one of their five highest. It was popular long ago, until they all agreed to stop using it, because combatants were farming crawlers to power it up. The necklace, Tipid says, is much worse than the ring.
beats.gist: King Rust's Necklace of Indelible Woe trades spells with a target; Tipid calls it worse than the ring.

beats.headline: In the dead king's pockets
beats.text: Walking the wrecked base with Boomer, Carl remembers: Donut has not really turned King Rust's body into a rug. Carl has him in his inventory. That means he now has a second Ring of Divine Suffering, and he has that damn necklace too. The dead king had several other magical items on him as well, most of which would not work on Carl. He will need to sit down with the others and talk about what to do with all of it.
beats.gist: Carl remembers King Rust's body is in his inventory, along with the necklace and a second ring.

beats.headline: We don't need that necklace
beats.text: Donut wants to know, in capitals, what Carl did with King Rust's ring and the necklace. Don't worry, he tells her. He can only wear one Ring of Divine Suffering at a time; he checked. Two rings cannot mark the same person on this floor anyway. And they do not need that necklace. The king had some other magical gear, which they will distribute around, and they will work out what to do with it all when there is time.
beats.gist: Carl tells Donut they do not need King Rust's necklace, since he can wear only one ring.

beats.headline: Li Na turns it down
beats.text: When Li Na first asked for Carl's spare Ring of Divine Suffering, his instinct was no. Imani agreed with him; Katia and Elle did not, and Donut, without saying why, begged him to give it to her as soon as he could. Li Na also asked about the Necklace of Indelible Woe, and then decided she did not want it, now that she has several level-15 dreads she could lose if she used it. It remains in Carl's inventory for now.
beats.gist: Li Na turns down the Necklace of Indelible Woe, so it stays with Carl.
